question: Let $f(x) = \log x$. Prove that $f(x)$ has no local maxima or minima for $x>0$.
explanation:
Compute derivative: f'(x) = 1/x.

Since 1/x > 0 for all x > 0, function is strictly increasing.

A strictly increasing function has no local maxima or minima.

options.A: $f(x)$ has a local maximum at $x=1$ because $f(1)=0$.
options.B: $f'(x)=\frac{1}{x}>0$ for all $x>0$, so $f(x)$ is strictly increasing and has no local maxima or minima.
options.C: $f'(x)=0$ at $x=1$, so $f(x)$ has a local minimum at $x=1$.
options.D: $f(x)$ has both a local maximum and a local minimum because it is defined for all $x>0$.
